build: E2c, part 1: the first fall frost in open ground, and a last picking for each place. In open ground (a garden open to frost that is not under cover) the first fall frost, with the garden's own frost days, ends the harvest of a frost-tender crop whose days would run past it, and what it would have picked after it is lost: the planting is picked to the frost day, its harvest days are those up to it, its yield follows them (a total over the days it was to be picked, or a week's figure for the weeks there are), and its ground is given back from the frost with its turnover. A crop cleared in one day loses nothing when it is ready before the frost, and all of it when it is ready after. A planting with a last day of its own stands over the frost and is picked to it (his word of Nov 18), still marked quietly as running past the first frost. Hardy crops are untouched, and so is anything under cover: tunnels, houses, and a crate or tower while it stands under shelter (towers in a garden open to frost are open ground). A crop picked to the season's end takes a last picking of its own for each place, kept on its line (assumptions.sell[crop].until, a month and day by place, taken with the line whole when two devices' plans meet); it stands for the season's end there in place of the frost, the year's end or the crop record's own day; in open ground a date past the frost is cut short by the frost, and anywhere a date past the day the garden closes ends on that day. On the crop's card the Last picking row then holds a date for each place, from the calendar, with whose day it is (your first frost, the first frost under cover, the year's end, yours) and, where the date is past the frost or the garden's close, that the frost or the close ends it sooner; a change shows what it moves first, as the harvest choice does, with one Undo. Picked for a set number of days, the card says the number once, in the Picked row, and Last picking gives only the dates it comes to. A planting cut by the frost says so among its notes. The farm dates window says that what a frost-tender crop would pick after the first fall frost is lost. The forecast kept for an engine follows each of these, since every change makes a new engine.

changes.did: In open ground the first fall frost now ends a frost-tender crop's harvest, and what it would pick after it is lost. A crop picked to the season's end takes a last-picking date for each place, on its card.
steps: Open Assumptions, Yield and price, and a tomato's card: Last picking shows a date in each place, with whose day it is (your first frost, the year's end).
Pick another date in the field: a sheet shows what moves and the season's worth before and after. Press Cancel and nothing changes.
On the Forecast, a frost-tender crop picked for a set number of days in the field stops on your first frost, and its total with it.
